info.title: Weft Ferrule service
info.description: `weft.ferrule-service.v1`: stateless Ferrule operations for horizontally scaled replicas. A route selects a trusted profile; the frame's own header selects the Ferrule operation within it. Over pinned mutual TLS the service also serves the `weft.inspection-transport.v1` routes, so an existing inspection client works unchanged. A separate plain probe listener, when configured, serves only the two health routes and answers `404` for every other path. Any other path answers `404`, and another method on a mapped path `405` with `Allow`.

post.description:
The service reads the complete frame before admission, so an incomplete frame never runs and its connection is aborted. An admitted operation answers `200` only after its child has settled; any other status means nothing ran. An operation identity is admitted once per replica. Send ready, the operation and its cancellation as streams of one HTTP/2 connection (pinned mutual TLS) or within one sandbox session, so that all reach the same replica.

| Profile | Request bytes | Response bytes | Wall seconds | CPU seconds | Memory bytes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edit` | 5259276 | 20971528 | 10 | 10 | 268435456 |
| `inspection` | 8388612 | 8388612 | 10 | 10 | 268435456 |
| `preview` | 12599368 | 9437444 | 30 | 30 | 536870912 |
| `compile` | 4210692 | 33686528 | 120 | 120 | 2147483648 |
| `execute` | 44040320 | 9437440 | 30 | 30 | 536870912 |

post.summary: Cancel an operation on the channel that carries it.
post.description: Cancels the admitted operation through its runner, which then answers it `200` with `Weft-Worker-Result: canceled`. A cancellation that arrives first is remembered, and the operation is answered `canceled` without running.

pinnedClientCertificate.description: Pinned mutual TLS: the TLS handshake completes only for a client certificate whose DER SHA-256 digest the service admits (`WEFT_FERRULE_SERVICE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_SHA256`), and the client pins the service certificate the same way. Trust stores, names and revocation are not used. A platform-sandbox deployment (`WEFT_FERRULE_SERVICE_AUTHENTICATION=platformSandbox`) instead listens on plain HTTP behind a platform front end that authenticates every caller and is the only route to the listener; it serves the service and probe routes only.
